result.title: MAEM: Mitigating Recency Bias via a Replay-Free, Capacity-Controlled Dynamic Mixture of Experts for Class-Incremental Graph Learning
result.summary: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) excel on graph-structured data but suffer catastrophic forgetting when classes arrive sequentially. In class-incremental graph learning, predictions are often dominated by recently learned classes, causing severe recency bias. Dynamic expansion can isolate knowledge across sessions, but many methods assume task-incremental settings and require task identities at test time to select branches or heads---information unavailable in class-incremental learning. Learnable routers offer an alternative, yet continual fine-tuning the router on new data can bias routing toward recent components. We propose MAEM, a replay-free, capacity-controlled dynamic mixture-of-experts framework for class-incremental graph learning. MAEM builds representations with Simplified Graph Convolution (SGC) and trains a dedicated expert for each new session, then freezes it to protect prior knowledge. For routing without task IDs or a shared trainable router, each expert uses a masked autoencoder (MAE); test nodes are assigned to the expert with the lowest reconstruction error, reducing routing-level recency bias. When the expert pool reaches a fixed capacity, MAEM merges the least-used experts via Git Re-Basin alignment and further distills them into a fused expert using topology-aware pseudo data synthesized from MAE distributions (DeepInversion-style), without storing or revisiting historical graph data. On four class-incremental graph benchmarks, MAEM mitigates recency bias, outperforms strong continual graph learning baselines, and keeps model capacity bounded under strict replay-free learning.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 MAEM：面向类别增量图学习，用 SGC 表示、每会话训练并冻结一个专家；测试时无需任务 ID，靠掩码自编码器的重建误差把节点分配给专家以缓解近因偏差，专家池满时用 Git Re-Basin 对齐合并少用专家并借伪数据蒸馏为融合专家，全程不回放历史图数据。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「以生成式重建误差在推理时无监督地选择专家」与容量受限下合并、蒸馏冗余专家的做法，可能为 LVR 中 latent 假设／计算分支的选择与状态复用提供方法线索，但领域为图增量学习，可迁移性尚待核查。
